https://english.pravda.ru/news/world/168.text: CIA Director John Ratcliffe Arrives in Moscow for Meetings With Russian Officials 25.08.2026 19:58 World CIA Director John Ratcliffe has arrived in Moscow for meetings with Russian officials, CBS and Axios said citing sources familiar with the visit. It is the first time Ratcliffe has traveled to Russia since becoming CIA director in January 2025. Ratcliffe arrives in Moscow aboard US military aircraft CBS reporter Jennifer Jacobs reported, citing sources, that Ratcliffe traveled to Moscow aboard a US Air Force C-17 military transport aircraft . Axios correspondent Barak Ravid also reported that two unnamed US officials had confirmed Ratcliffe's visit. The sources described the purpose of the trip simply as "meetings in Moscow." No further details about the agenda or the Russian officials Ratcliffe is expected to meet have been disclosed. Later, flight-tracking data showed that the US Air Force Boeing C-17 Globemaster III with the registration RCH4555 had departed Moscow's Vnukovo Airport and was heading toward Riga. The aircraft's arrival initially raised questions Information about Ratcliffe's visit emerged after a US Air Force Boeing C-17A Globemaster III was spotted at Vnukovo, along with what CBS described as an American diplomatic motorcade. Neither Washington nor Moscow initially disclosed the identity of the senior US official who had arrived or the purpose of the visit. According to Flightradar24 data, the aircraft departed Riga at approximately 8:50 a. m. Moscow time and landed at Vnukovo at about 10:04 a. m. on August 25. Two days earlier, on August 23, the aircraft had flown to Riga from Camp Springs, Maryland, where Andrews Air Force Base is located. Air Force One is among the aircraft based there. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov later said he had no information about the arrival of the American aircraft. Ratcliffe's first Moscow visit as CIA director John Ratcliffe became director of the US Central Intelligence Agency on January 23, 2025. Previously, from May 2020 to January 2021, he served as US director of national intelligence, becoming the first person to head both agencies. Ratcliffe has received the National Security Medal and the US Department of Defense Medal for Distinguished Public Service. According to Axios , his trip is the first visit to Moscow by Ratcliffe since taking office and the highest-level visit to Russia by a representative of the Donald Trump administration since January. Washington reportedly asked Kyiv to avoid strikes during visit The reports of Ratcliffe's arrival came amid information that Washington had asked Kyiv to refrain from carrying out strikes against Moscow, St. Petersburg and Russia's northern regions between August 24 and 26. The Financial Times reporter Christopher Miller, citing sources, reported that representatives of US President Donald Trump had made the request. According to the FT sources, Washington explained that it planned to send a senior American official to Moscow by aircraft. Ukraine agreed not to carry out strikes during the specified period. CIA's role in US-Russia prisoner exchanges CBS noted that the CIA was involved in several recent prisoner exchanges between Russia and the United States. The agency participated in the April 2025 release of US and Russian citizen Ksenia Karelina, whose case Ratcliffe personally handled, as well as the 2024 exchange that brought Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich and former US Marine Paul Whelan back to the United States. Previous CIA chief visited Moscow in 2021 The previous CIA director, William Burns , visited Moscow in November 2021. During that trip, he met with Russian officials, including then-Security Council Secretary Nikolai Patrushev and Foreign Intelligence Service Director Sergey Naryshkin. Burns also spoke by telephone with President Vladimir Putin. According to CNN , the discussions at the time focused on the movement of Russian troops and military equipment near Ukraine's northern border. Ratcliffe's arrival therefore marks a significant new high-level US contact with Moscow, although the precise agenda of his meetings and the issues discussed remain undisclosed. https://www.americanthinker.com/blog/202.text: Foreign Policy > Putin Link copied Putin doesnât have to invade NATO to attack it Weakened Russian leader may not be testing NATO’s military strength, but its definition of an “attack.” Greg Richter | August 31, 2026 Kaupo Rosin, the head of Estonia’s Foreign Intelligence Service, says we should stop using the phrase “hybrid warfare.” “Hybrid schmybrid,” he told the Telegraph , dismissing a term that he says sanitizes what Russia is actually doing: “sabotage, unconventional activities, cyber attacks and information warfare.” Some of it, he said, could more accurately be described as state-sponsored terrorism. Americans tend to imagine a Russian attack on NATO as tanks rolling across the Estonian border or missiles raining down on Poland. That might be the kind of attack Vladimir Putin has no intention of launching. President Donald Trump said last week that Putin would not attack NATO territory. And NATO itself said Sunday that it sees no imminent threat of a conventional Russian attack, but that’s not the same thing as saying Russia is leaving NATO alone. NATO acknowledges an increase in Russian “hybrid acts” across Europe. Germany, for example, is investigating a suspected drone attack involving explosives near a Ukrainian cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle airport. German officials have described it as a possible hybrid attack, although they have not publicly attributed it to Russia. Meanwhile, CIA Director John Ratcliffe recently made a rare trip to Moscow to meet his Russian counterpart. According to Reuters , Ratcliffe raised concerns about the possibility of Russian operations against a NATO member. And so, how much sabotage, cyberwarfare or deniable violence constitutes an attack? NATO says Article 5 is not restricted to tanks, bombs and invading armies. A significant cyberattack or other hybrid attack can qualify as an “armed attack,” but the determination is made case by case. NATO has good reason not to publish an exact threshold since that would tell Moscow exactly how far it could go without triggering collective defense. But Moscow still can test that threshold. Putin does not need to conquer Estonia; he merely needs to discover how much disruption, intimidation and destruction NATO countries will tolerate while arguing among themselves about whether they have actually been attacked. That’s not all. Rosin says dissatisfaction with the Ukraine war is spreading through Russian society, including among oligarchs and others with access to “money, weapons and information.” He does not predict Putin’s imminent downfall, but says any political change could come suddenly. A weakened leader with few good options at home may have greater incentive to demonstrate strength abroad. The danger, then, may not be that Putin wakes up one morning and orders an invasion of NATO. It is that he keeps attacking NATO in ways carefully designed to make NATO wonder whether it has been attacked at all. https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: Police patrol outside the Heaton Park synagogue in Manchester as the Jewish community marks Yom Kippur on 21 September 2026. Photograph: Christopher Furlong/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Police patrol outside the Heaton Park synagogue in Manchester as the Jewish community marks Yom Kippur on 21 September 2026. Photograph: Christopher Furlong/Getty Images UK security and counter-terrorism Police believe they have foiled ‘imminent’ attack on Manchester’s Jewish community Counter-terrorism police say ‘long-running investigation’ disrupted alleged plot days after two men arrested on eve of the holy day Yom Kippur Vikram Dodd Police and crime correspondent Tue 22 Sep 2026 13.50 EDT Last modified on Tue 22 Sep 2026 15.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Police believe they have stopped an imminent plot to attack Jewish communities in the Manchester area. The announcement on Tuesday follows the arrest of two men on Sunday at 2.45pm in Manchester and comes during the Jewish holy month. Counter-terrorism investigators were unusually explicit about the alleged attack plot, which was halted after an operation lasting several months. Police believe they have detained the main suspects and any materials they may have been planning to use. Deputy assistant commissioner Vicki Evans, senior national coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, said: “This has been a long-running proactive investigation which has led to the disruption of what we believe to be a plot to target the Jewish community in the Manchester area.” The arrests and official confirmation of a suspected attack plot comes almost a year after an Islamist-incited attack on a Manchester synagogue on Yom Kippur left two people dead, with the attacker shot dead by police. Arrests were made hours before this year’s Yom Kippur started, with police fearing any plot might be “imminent”. The Jewish festival of Sukkot falls on Friday, with other holy days to follow. Evans added: “We are acutely aware this news will cause further concern to the Jewish community, as well as the wider public, especially given the significant High Holy Day period. “I want to reassure them we are working incredibly closely with colleagues in Greater Manchester police and partners to ensure we’re doing everything we can to keep them and the wider public safe.” The two men in their 30s were arrested under section 41 of the Terrorism Act, meaning police suspected they were terrorists. Police will not officially say what the motive was, nor the nationality or ethnicity of those detained. The Guardian understands that a far-right motive is thought to be unlikely. Sources stress the investigation is at an early stage. Islamist extremism is among possible motives under consideration, and given a spate of recent attacks against Jewish targets, investigators are searching for any sign of a state link. Investigators are increasingly finding it difficult to determine motive until much later in an investigation, if at all. The UK’s terrorism threat level is now at its second highest level of severe. The investigation was led by CTP in London and the two men arrested have been taken to a police station in the capital for questioning. Warrants for their further detention have been granted, meaning they can be held until Sunday. The arrests led to searches in Epworth Street, Liverpool, and Lancaster Road, Salford, which police say have now been completed. Examination of electronic devices such as mobile phones is under way. Evans added: “Counter Terrorism Policing continue to focus our efforts on identifying and disrupting those who wish to cause harm in our communities. “As we have shown with these arrests, where we suspect there could be a threat to the public, then we will not hesitate to investigate and take action. “We are pursuing a number of lines of inquiry and we anticipate these will continue over the coming days as this investigation continues. “Importantly, we do not believe there to be any ongoing threat to the public in relation to this matter, but as ever, we would ask that people remain vigilant and contact police with any concerns.” The Community Security Trust (CST), which works to keep Jewish communities in the UK safe from attack, said: “This is utterly chilling, coming so close to the anniversary of the terrorist attack at Heaton Park Synagogue last year, and is another reminder of the serious terrorist threat facing Jewish communities in this current time. “We urge the Jewish community to remain calm and alert, and to report any suspicious activity to police on 999 and then to CST.” Explore more on these topics UK security and counter-terrorism Manchester Religion news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c51k.text: Image source, Presidential handout Image caption, South Africa President Cyril Ramaphosa By Henry Moore BBC News Published 4 hours ago South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa on Tuesday announced a clean-up of high-risk areas across the country, after the bodies of 12 women were discovered in an area east of Johannesburg in just two months. The deaths sparked a national outcry about the scale of violence against women in South Africa, which has one of the highest rates of gender-based violence in the world. Ramaphosa announced what he called a multidisciplinary, national-level emergency response to the murders, for which there have been four arrests. He said gender-based violence "cannot be accepted as a normal part of life in South Africa" and admitted the country has "not done enough" to protect women and girls. "There has understandably been widespread fear that the discovery of these women in close proximity could indicate the work of a single perpetrator," Ramaphosa said in an address to the nation. "At present, the police have not found evidence establishing that these killings were committed by a single perpetrator." Admitting the government has not done enough in recent years to prevent gender-based violence, he announced a new wave of measures to help protect women and girls. "Every municipality must begin a women's safety audit without delay," he said. "High-risk areas must be identified" and addressed. "These audits must identify broken streetlights, overgrown public spaces, abandoned buildings, unsafe transport routes and facilities, poorly secured parks, and other conditions that place women at risk." Ramaphosa also announced an "enforcement package" to reduce alcohol-related violence. "Alcohol does not cause gender-based violence and it can never excuse it. Responsibility always lies with the perpetrator," he said. "But harmful alcohol use is a significant aggravating factor in interpersonal violence, and it must be addressed as part of our wider prevention effort." The South African president also said a deeper change, beyond policing and legislation, must take place to reduce violence against women and girls, saying it "does not begin when a fist is raised" or when a woman is raped or murdered. "It begins much earlier," he said. "It begins in attitudes that regard women as inferiorâ¦ with the belief that a man has the right to control a woman. "It begins when jealousy is mistaken for love, when control is mistaken for protection and coercion is mistaken for affection. "It begins when a man refuses to accept the word no." He went on to call on men and boys to take the lead in ending gender-based violence. "We have placed the burden of male violence on women," Ramaphosa said. "That must change." "The solution to violence against women cannot be to make women less free." South Africa has one of the highest homicide rates, with 5,427 people murdered between April and June this year alone. While South African police statistics do not differentiate victims by gender, the South African Human Rights Commission said recently that 569 women were killed and 1,052 others survived attempted murder between April and June this year. https://www.politico.eu/article/lukasz-g.text: Independent Łukasz Gibała won Kraków’s mayoral runoff on Sunday, defeating a candidate backed by Prime Minister Donald Tusk and handing Poland’s governing Civic Coalition a setback in the country’s second-largest city. Gibała secured 61% of the vote against 39% for Senator Monika Piątkowska, according to an exit poll published just after polling stations closed at 9 p.m. local time. Turnout was 44.7%; complete results are expected overnight into Monday. The result follows the removal of Mayor Aleksander Miszalski, backed by Civic Coalition, in a May referendum. Advertisement Advertisement “The people of Kraków have just regained their city! Now let’s put aside our differences and show that we can work together,” Gibała said, appearing to acknowledge that he will have to cooperate with Civic Coalition and its national coalition partner, the Left party, which together control 23 of the city council’s 43 seats. This was Gibała’s fourth shot at the mayoralty. A local councilor and former national lawmaker, Gibała narrowly lost to Miszalski in 2024 in his previous attempt. This time around, he campaigned on breaking with the political establishment, riding a wave of public discontent over Kraków’s huge debt and attempts to establish a low-emissions zone. Gibała won the Sept. 27 first round with 36.4% ahead of Piątkowska on 29.9%. The candidate of the main opposition Law and Justice party finished third with 17.5%. Piątkowska, backed by Civic Coalition, tried to distance herself from Miszalski while arguing that close ties with the national government would benefit Kraków, pop. 800,000. Nationally, Civic Coalition remains ahead in opinion polls, but current voting intentions suggest that Tusk’s coalition will fall short of a majority in scheduled fall parliamentary elections. Two October surveys listed by polling aggregator ewybory.eu put Civic Coalition at 31.9%, Law and Order at 17.7%, the far-right Confederation at 14% and another far-right grouping, the Confederation of the Polish Crown, at 8.3%. Of Civic Coalition’s three government allies, only the Left, at 7%, would exceed the 5% threshold for parliamentary representation, dimming the administration’s prospects of retaining power.
